We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =3x+2 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =3 \\ \text{d}u & =3\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u & =\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=3x+2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 2 \\ u & 5 & 8\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{5}^{8}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{8}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{5}^{8}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{5}^{8} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$
